hints: A directed graph is strongly connected when every city can reach every other city.
Pick city 1 and search forward; then search the reversed graph from 1.
If either search misses a city, that direction gives a concrete counterexample pair.
analogy: Check whether everyone is reachable from one hub in both the original and reversed road directions.
example: If 1 reaches 2 but 2 cannot reach 1, the reversed search from 1 misses 2, proving the network is not strongly connected.
algorithm: Run DFS/BFS from vertex 1 in original and reversed graphs. If original misses v, print NO and 1 v; if reversed misses v, print NO and v 1; otherwise YES.
correctness: Strong connectivity implies both reachability searches cover all nodes. If both cover all nodes, any u reaches 1 in the reverse-check sense and 1 reaches v, giving u->v.
